title: Understanding Gradient Descent
text: Gradient descent is an optimization algorithm used to minimize a function by iteratively moving towards the steepest descent direction. It is commonly used in machine learning to find the optimal parameters for a model.

title: Global vs. Local Minimum
text: A global minimum is the lowest point in the entire domain of a function, while a local minimum is the lowest point in a specific region. Gradient descent aims to find the global minimum, but it may get stuck in a local minimum depending on the function's shape.

title: Role of Learning Rate
text: The learning rate determines the size of the steps taken towards the minimum. A fixed learning rate can affect the convergence of gradient descent. If it's too large, it might overshoot the minimum; if too small, it might take too long to converge.

title: Convergence of Gradient Descent
text: Consider the statement: 'With an infinite number of updates and a fixed learning rate, gradient descent will always converge to a global minimum.' Is this statement true or false?
